# Sirach Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_020_page_001.jpg

---

**20:1** There is a rebuke that is not timely; and there is a person who is wise to be silent.

**20:2** How much better it is to reprove than to be angry; and one who confesses will be kept back from failure.

**20:3** Like a eunuch who lusts to violate a young woman, so is the person who does right by force.

**20:4** There is one who keeps silent because he lacks knowledge, and there is one who keeps silent because he knows when to wait.

**20:5** A wise man will be silent until the right moment, but a boastful fool misses the right time.

**20:6** One who talks too much is detested, and one who takes authority for himself is hated.

**20:7** There is good fortune for a man in adversity, and gain in loss.

**20:8** There is a gift that does not profit you, and there is a gift that is given twice over.

**20:9** There are humiliations on account of glory, and there is one who lifts up his head from a low estate.

**20:10** There is one who buys much for little, and pays for it seven times over.

**20:11** A wise man with words makes himself loved; but the gracious speech of fools is wasted.

**20:12** A gift from a fool will not profit you; for he has many eyes instead of one.

**20:13** He gives little and upbraids much; he opens his mouth like a herald — who can be grateful for such a thing?

**20:14** Today a man borrows, tomorrow he asks again; such a person is hateful to God and to man.

**20:15** A fool will say, "I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds"; those who eat his bread are evil-tongued.

**20:16** How many times and how many will laugh at him?

**20:17** Better to slip on the floor than to slip with the tongue; the downfall of the wicked will come quickly.

**20:18** A graceless person is like a tale told at the wrong time; it will often be on the lips of the uneducated.

**20:19** A proverb from a fool's mouth will be rejected, for he does not utter it at the proper season.

**20:20** There is one whose poverty prevents him from sinning; and when he rests, he feels no remorse.

**20:21** There is one who is destroyed because of his modesty; he is ruined by a fool's judgment.

**20:22** There is one who is promised something in friendship, and he makes him his enemy without cause.

**20:23** Blame covers a person with shame; and blame from one who is jealous misrepresents.

**20:24** A lie is an evil blot on a person; it is continually in the mouth of the uneducated.

**20:25** A thief is preferable to a habitual liar, but both are heading for destruction.

**20:26** Dishonor belongs to the liar; his shame is always with him.

**20:27** A wise man advances himself through his speech, and an intelligent person pleases the great.

**20:28** Whoever tills his land will pile up his harvest, and whoever pleases the great will atone for injustice.

**20:29** Gifts and presents blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up their ears like a muzzle.

**20:30** Hidden wisdom and concealed treasure — what profit is there in either of them?

**20:31** Better is the man who hides his folly than the man who hides his wisdom.
